ip_top_stories.title: Appeals court upholds Thomson Reuters' landmark win in AI training lawsuit
ip_top_stories.summary: A US appeals court has upheld Thomson Reuters' victory in its lawsuit concerning the use of Westlaw headnotes to train an AI competitor. The ruling reinforces the earlier finding that such use of copyrighted legal content does not constitute fair use, marking a significant precedent for AI training data and copyright law.

ip_top_stories.title: Trump's DoJ was biased and wrong about 'fair use', say news orgs in OpenAI dispute
ip_top_stories.summary: News organisations have filed court submissions urging a judge to disregard the US Department of Justice's position backing OpenAI's fair use defence in copyright litigation. The publishers argue the DOJ's stance is biased toward AI companies and misrepresents copyright law as it applies to training data.

ip_top_stories.title: New Code, Old Rules: 9th Circuit Says GitHub Copilot's Output Is Not a 'Copy' Under the DMCA
ip_top_stories.summary: The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals has ruled that output generated by GitHub Copilot does not constitute a 'copy' under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act. The decision has significant implications for how AI-generated code is treated under existing copyright frameworks.

ip_top_stories.title: Operator of AI music generator can't escape copyright suit
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has declined to dismiss a copyright infringement lawsuit against the operator of an AI music generator, allowing the case to proceed. The ruling is an important development for how copyright law applies to AI systems that generate musical content.

ip_top_stories.title: OpenAI Used Pirated Books for AI Training Despite Knowing Illegality, Court Filings Reveal Executive Statements
ip_top_stories.summary: Court filings have revealed executive statements indicating that OpenAI knowingly used pirated books to train its AI models. The disclosures, surfaced during ongoing litigation, could significantly affect the company's legal position in multiple copyright cases.

ip_further_links.title: Hong Kong delays AI copyright law to focus on guidelines first
ip_further_links.summary: Hong Kong authorities have announced a delay to planned AI copyright legislation, opting instead to issue guidelines as an interim measure while broader legal reform is considered.

ip_further_links.title: As Publishers Ramp Up AI Implementation, Employees Slow Down [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers Weekly reports that as publishing companies accelerate AI adoption, employee engagement and uptake of AI tools is lagging, creating tension between corporate strategy and workforce practice.

ip_further_links.title: De Marque to Offer AI Audiobook Capabilities Via ElevenLabs [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Publishing technology company De Marque has announced a partnership with ElevenLabs to integrate AI-generated audiobook capabilities into its platform.

ip_further_links.title: Who owns your face? India's legal battle over AI and personality rights
ip_further_links.summary: Indian courts are grappling with legal questions around personality rights and AI-generated likenesses, as cases emerge testing how existing law applies to the use of individuals' faces and identities by AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: Back to the eighties… who owns your AI-generated retro self?
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of emerging intellectual property questions around AI-generated images styled after individuals' likenesses, examining who holds rights over such output.

ip_further_links.title: Nvidia settles trademark lawsuit over 'Modulus' AI software
ip_further_links.summary: Nvidia has reached a settlement in a trademark dispute concerning the name 'Modulus' used for one of its AI software products.

ip_further_links.title: Are Libraries Prepared for the Second Digital Transformation of Distinctive Collections?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines whether libraries have the resources and strategies in place to manage AI-driven digitisation pressures on their unique and distinctive collections.

ip_further_links.title: Scholastic Agrees to Buy Cottage Door Press for $71 Million [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Scholastic has announced an agreement to acquire children's publisher Cottage Door Press for $71 million, expanding its early childhood publishing portfolio.
